heading: Sockets
body: SocketRoute marks a controller that keeps a WebSocket open at its path. Put the class in server/controllers/ in any Yon language (.js, .ts, .py, .go, .java, .kt, .cs, .fs, .php, .rb, .rs or .dart). Tachyon makes one object for each connection, as Jakarta's @ServerEndpoint does. OnOpen runs when a browser connects, OnMessage runs for each message, OnClose runs when the socket closes, and OnError runs when OnOpen or OnMessage fails; the socket stays open, as in Jakarta. The session sends messages back, closes the socket, and lists the open sessions of the same path with openSessions() (each language uses its own style, such as open_sessions() in Python). Each message is JSON text of at most 64 KiB, and Tachyon checks it against the model type of the OnMessage parameter. When the browser closes the socket, Tachyon answers with the same close code, so the browser sees a clean close. SocketRequest on an HTTPClient method receives the messages in the browser, and the client's send(message) sends one. Public, SignedIn or Allow(Role) on the SocketRoute class says who may connect. Tachyon checks it before it opens the socket, and answers 401 or 403 instead.
